content: The Tribunal of Ancona resolved a dispute regarding the "convenient divisibility" of a residential property under Article 720 of the Civil Code. The judge scrutinized a fragmentation project that would have split the apartment into two smaller units. It was determined that such a division was structurally and economically unfeasible due to high renovation costs. Specifically, the project required €52,813 in works, representing nearly 30% of the total property value. Furthermore, the division would have imposed excessive servitudes and utility dependencies, compromising autonomous enjoyment. Legal issues also included the timeliness of the defendant's request for division instead of sale. The court ruled that changing the defense strategy at the final hearing was procedurally inadmissible. Ultimately, the property was ordered for auction as the only viable method for liquidation.
